rounds.fact: Wikipedia's interface has stayed remarkably close to its original look for two decades. The visual restraint was intentional, to keep the focus on editing and content rather than design.
Star ratings lasted until 2010. They were retired because almost everyone rated either 5 stars or 1, so the site switched to thumbs up/down.
Pinterest launched by invite-only in 2010, and its signature masonry grid of pins was one of the first mainstream uses of that layout style on the web.
Slack was built from the internal chat tool of Glitch, a whimsical MMO that shut down in 2012. The aubergine sidebar became so iconic that its 2019 rebrand made headlines.
Amazon started as an online bookstore in 1994. By 1999 the homepage was already a dense grid of categories and personalized recommendations, a layout philosophy it never really abandoned.
